events.title: Sumatra-Andaman earthquake and Indian Ocean tsunami, 2004
events.why: The tsunami crossed the Bay of Bengal and reached the coast you live on. Many measurements exist, so the challenge is choosing the strongest evidence, not finding some.

sources.title: Earthquake summary map: M9.1 Sumatra-Andaman Islands, 26 December 2004 (PDF)
sources.use: A tectonic setting map with the plates named and how fast they move. Start your Where and Cause sections here.

sources.title: Tsunami Generation from the 2004 M=9.1 Sumatra-Andaman Earthquake
sources.publisher: USGS Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center
sources.use: Why this earthquake made such a large tsunami. Read it before you draw your diagram.

sources.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami Remembered
sources.use: Scientists look back at what the tsunami did and what they learned from it.

sources.title: Impact of Tsunami 2004 in Coastal Villages of Nagapattinam District, India (PDF)
sources.use: Run-up heights and how far the sea came inland on the Tamil Nadu coast. Useful for your Effect section.

sources.title: Tsunami Ready
sources.publisher: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)
sources.use: India's tsunami warning center and community preparedness program. Start your Solutions section here.

questions.cause: Which plate is sinking beneath which? Use the summary map to find the direction and speed of each plate.
questions.effect: How long did the tsunami take to reach different coasts, and why did some places flood farther inland than others?
questions.solution: What can India's warning system do now that nobody could do in 2004? What can it still not do?

events.watch: The USGS gives the magnitude as 9.1; other sources say 9.1 to 9.3. Say which source you used. Death tolls also differ by source and by the year they were published.

events.title: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, 2011
events.why: Japan was one of the best-prepared countries in the world, and the tsunami still went over many of its defenses. A good choice for a poster that asks whether the solutions worked.

sources.title: M 9.1: 2011 Great Tohoku Earthquake, Japan
sources.use: Location, depth, shaking maps and a tectonic summary that names the plates.

sources.title: On This Day: 2011 Japan Earthquake and Tsunami
sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.use: NOAA's summary from its tsunami database, including wave height and cost.

sources.title: Lessons Learned from the 2011 Great East Japan Tsunami: Performance of Tsunami Countermeasures, Coastal Buildings, and Tsunami Evacuation in Japan (PDF)
sources.use: A research paper on which seawalls, breakwaters and evacuation plans held and which failed. Read the abstract and the conclusions first.

sources.title: Massive 2011 Tohoku earthquake spurred development of modern tsunami forecast systems
sources.use: How tsunami forecasting changed because of this event.

sources.title: Japan Impacts from the 2011 Tohoku Earthquake and Tsunami
sources.use: A map tour of the coast. It contains images and video of the tsunami.

questions.cause: Which two plates meet off northeast Japan, and what kind of fault moved?
questions.effect: Why did the tsunami cause far more deaths than the shaking did?
questions.solution: Pick one defense: a seawall, a breakwater or an evacuation route. Did it work in 2011? What evidence tells you?

events.watch: Early reports gave the magnitude as 8.9 or 9.0; the USGS figure is now 9.1. The nuclear accident is a big topic of its own. Keep it to one part of your poster, or the plate tectonics gets lost.

events.title: Great Alaska earthquake, 1964
events.why: The second-largest earthquake ever recorded with instruments. Studying it helped scientists understand subduction zones, so the history of the science is part of the story.

sources.title: M 9.2: The 1964 Prince William Sound, Alaska Earthquake
sources.use: The official location, depth and magnitude, with links to maps and photos.

sources.title: The 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake and Tsunamis: A Modern Perspective and Enduring Legacies (Fact Sheet 2014-3018)
sources.use: A short summary of what happened and what changed afterward.

sources.title: 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake and Tsunami
sources.use: Videos and photos, including a talk by the geologist who first explained the earthquake as a subduction event.

sources.title: Great Alaska Earthquake
sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.use: How the disaster led to a new tsunami warning center. Start your Solutions section here.

questions.cause: How did the land move during the earthquake? Look for places that rose and places that sank.
questions.effect: Most deaths came from tsunamis, not from shaking. Where did those tsunamis come from?
questions.solution: What does a tsunami warning center do that did not exist in 1964? How fast can a warning go out now?

events.watch: Death counts differ between sources, for example 128 and 131. Times are given in Alaska time or in UTC, which puts the date on 27 or 28 March. Both are right; say which you use.

events.title: Great Hanshin (Kobe) earthquake, 1995
events.setting: Fault beneath a city, near a subduction zone
events.why: A modern city whose building rules had changed several times before the earthquake. A good choice for a poster about why some buildings fail and others survive.

sources.title: Reference sheet: the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake (PDF)
sources.publisher: International Institute of Seismology and Earthquake Engineering, Building Research Institute, Japan
sources.use: Damage figures and building lessons from Japan's own building research institute.

sources.title: Special Publication 901: the 1995 Hyogoken-Nanbu (Kobe) earthquake (PDF)
sources.publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.use: A long engineering report. Use the contents page to find the section on buildings and building law.

sources.title: 1995 Kobe earthquake, Japan
sources.use: What happened to the port when the ground liquefied.

sources.title: Lessons from the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake (PDF)
sources.use: Japan's own summary of what it changed after 1995.

sources.title: Kobe Earthquake
sources.use: A short overview to read first.

questions.cause: Kobe is on land, not on a trench. Which fault moved, and how is it connected to the plates around Japan?
questions.effect: Which buildings collapsed and which did not? Look for the year each was built.
questions.solution: What did Japan change after 1995, and how would you know whether it worked?

events.watch: The magnitude is 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale and 7.2 or 7.3 on other scales. These are different scales, not a disagreement. Say which scale you use.

events.title: Bhuj (Gujarat) earthquake, 2001
events.setting: Inside a plate, away from the boundary
events.why: An earthquake in India, far from any plate edge. Explaining why it happened at all is the puzzle, so this is a strong choice if you like a challenge.

sources.title: 26 January 2001 Bhuj earthquake, Gujarat, India
sources.use: Fault maps, an earlier earthquake in the same region in 1819, and notes on intensity. It is a researcher's working page, so check its dates.

sources.title: The Mw 7.7 Bhuj earthquake: Global lessons for earthquake hazard in intra-plate regions
sources.publisher: Schweig and others, U.S. Geological Survey
sources.use: Why earthquakes inside plates are hard to plan for. Read the abstract.

sources.title: Initial Geotechnical Observations of the Bhuj, India, Earthquake of January 26, 2001
sources.use: A field team's report on ground failure, dams, ports and bridges.

sources.title: Bhuj, January 26, 2001, M7.7 Earthquake
sources.use: Reconnaissance reports, a recovery report and photos.

sources.title: Rising up from the ashes: Gujarat ramps up disaster preparedness
sources.use: The disaster management institutions Gujarat set up after 2001. Start your Solutions section here.

questions.cause: If Bhuj is not on a plate boundary, where did the stress come from? Which plate is pushing on which?
questions.effect: Why was damage reported far from the epicenter, in cities such as Ahmedabad?
questions.solution: What did Gujarat set up after 2001? Would it help in the next earthquake?

events.watch: Death tolls range from about 13,800 to over 20,000, depending on the source and when it was written. The magnitude is given as 7.6 or 7.7. Report the range and its sources, not one number.

events.title: Tangshan earthquake, 1976
events.why: One of the deadliest earthquakes in recorded history, inside a plate, in a city nobody had marked as high risk. This tab has the hardest source work on the list.

sources.title: The Great Tangshan Earthquake of 1976 (EERL Report 2002-001)
sources.publisher: Liu, Housner, Xie and He (editors), California Institute of Technology
sources.use: A full engineering report, free to download. Use the table of contents. Do not try to read it all.

sources.title: Tangshan earthquake of 1976
sources.use: A short overview. An encyclopedia is a place to start, not a source of data.

sources.title: Tangshan earthquake
sources.use: Compare the magnitude it gives with the Caltech report and the case study card. Why might they differ?

sources.title: Global Significant Earthquake Database
sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.use: Search for Tangshan to see the database record for deaths and damage.

questions.cause: Tangshan is about 1,000 km from the nearest plate boundary. What could build up stress there?
questions.effect: Why did the time of day and the type of buildings matter so much?
questions.solution: What did China change after 1976? Use the 2008 Sichuan earthquake to judge whether it worked.

events.watch: The official death toll and outside estimates differ by hundreds of thousands. The magnitude is given anywhere from 7.5 to 8.0. Never use one number without saying where it came from.

events.title: Pinatubo eruption, 1991
events.why: The second-largest eruption of the 20th century. Scientists forecast it and people were evacuated, and the danger went on for years afterward.

sources.title: The Cataclysmic 1991 Eruption of Mount Pinatubo, Philippines (Fact Sheet 113-97)
sources.use: What happened, the warning signs and the effects, in two pages.

sources.title: Lahars of Mount Pinatubo, Philippines (Fact Sheet 114-97)
sources.use: Why rain turned the ash into mudflows that kept burying villages.

sources.title: Pinatubo
sources.use: The eruption record and the tectonic setting.

sources.title: Pinatubo 25 Years Later: Eight Ways the Eruption Broke Ground
sources.use: How the eruption changed the way scientists respond to volcanic crises.

questions.cause: Which plate is sinking beneath Luzon, and how does that produce magma that explodes?
questions.effect: Why did roofs collapse, and why did lahars keep happening long after the eruption ended?
questions.solution: What warning signs did scientists watch, and how did they decide when to evacuate?

events.watch: Pinatubo also cooled global temperatures for a while. That is real, but keep it short: your poster is about the plate setting and the local hazard.

events.title: Merapi eruption, 2010
events.why: One of Indonesia's most active volcanoes, with hundreds of thousands of people living on and around it. A story about forecasting and hard evacuation decisions.

sources.title: Merapi
sources.use: The eruption record, the tectonic setting and how many people live nearby.

sources.title: Successful Crisis Response by Indonesia's First-Class Volcano Response Team
sources.use: How the evacuation zone was decided in 2010. Start your Solutions section here.

sources.title: The 2010 explosive eruption of Java's Merapi volcano: a '100-year' event
sources.publisher: Surono and others, U.S. Geological Survey record
sources.use: The scientific paper. Read the abstract for the warning signs and the numbers.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Volcano Monitoring in Indonesia
sources.use: How Indonesian and U.S. scientists monitor the volcano.

questions.cause: Which plate is sinking beneath Java? How does a lava dome grow and then collapse?
questions.effect: Why are pyroclastic flows so much deadlier than lava flows?
questions.solution: How did scientists decide how far to move people? What did moving cost the people who left?

events.watch: Merapi erupts often, including in recent years. Check that every source you use is about 2010, not another eruption.

events.title: Pompeii and Herculaneum, 79 CE
events.why: No instruments existed, so the evidence is ash layers, buried towns and one eyewitness who wrote it down. The same volcano is still active, with hundreds of thousands of people living around it.

sources.title: Pliny the Younger, Letters 6.16 and 6.20 (translated by Cynthia Damon)
sources.use: The only eyewitness account. Use it as evidence, and do its OPVL carefully: who wrote it, when, and why?

sources.title: Vesuvius
sources.use: The eruption record and the tectonic setting.

sources.title: Vesuvius
sources.publisher: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia (INGV), Italy
sources.use: How Italy's national volcano institute describes and monitors Vesuvius today.

sources.title: Are you prepared? Volcanic risk at Vesuvius
sources.use: Today's plan for the people around Vesuvius. Start your Solutions section here.

sources.title: Map of National Emergency Planning for Vesuvius
sources.use: The red and yellow zones on a map.

questions.cause: Which plate is sinking beneath southern Italy? Check more than one source, because they do not all describe it the same way.
questions.effect: How did people die in Herculaneum compared with Pompeii? What evidence tells us?
questions.solution: Nothing could be done in 79 CE. What is the plan now for the people who live around Vesuvius, and could it work?

events.watch: The date is debated: many sources say 24 August, and newer evidence points to October. AI tools often give August as certain. AI tools also invent lines from Pliny's letters, so quote only from the letters themselves.

shared.title: Natural Hazards: tsunamis, earthquakes and volcanoes
shared.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
shared.use: Searchable databases and an interactive map of significant earthquakes, tsunamis and eruptions. Every event on this page is in it.

choose.challenge: Many sources, so the work is choosing the best. The tsunami reached the Chennai coast.
Rich Solutions part: some defenses held and some did not.
An older event. How scientists came to understand it is part of the story.
Linking a fault under a city to the bigger plate picture takes care.
"Which boundary?" has no simple answer. Good if you like a puzzle.
Fewer English sources, and the numbers are disputed. The hardest source work.
A forecast and an evacuation, then hazards that lasted for years.
Forecasting and evacuation decisions under pressure.
No instruments, so the evidence is deposits, ruins and one eyewitness.
